label: Early original-phase steps (t<=2) on/after tokens x,e,g,z,f,0
explanation: Fires almost only in the first few original-phase input steps: 99.5% of activation mass is in the original phase and 94% at t<=2 (t=1 holds 44% of mass, t=2 31%, t=0 19%). It is essentially silent from t>=4, at the delimiter, and in the copy phase. Within t<=2 it depends on which tokens came in: it is strongest when the current input is one of x, e, g, z, f, 0 (rates of 15-18% versus about 5% overall), or when the previous input was f, x, 0, r or e. The largest activations come at t=2 on e or x right after f, e.g. 0 f e / 0 f x / f f e. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of a token (92% of mass). The token-set predicate is only an approximation of what looks like a token-combination-dependent hidden state in the first 2-3 steps. Many steps that match the token sets stay inactive, and some other combinations (e.g. n then r, h then n) also fire, so precision is around 0.6.
